question.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & -2 & -2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z=1 \\ 0x+y+z=1 \\ 0x+0y+0z=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Since any numbers $x,y,z$ form a solution of the final equation $0x+0y+0z=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of just two equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+2y+3z=1 \\ y+z=1\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. In this case, the basic variables are $x$ and $y,$ and we have one free variable, $z.$ That means we need to find $x$ and $y$ in terms of $z.$ To do this, we apply the back substitution. 

From the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+z=1\,⇒\,y=1-z\end{aligned}
$$

and substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2(1-z)+3z=1\,⇒\,x=-1-z\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the general solution is

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=-1-z \\ y=1-z \\ z=z\end{aligned}
$$

where $z$ (free variable) is an arbitrary number.

In vector form, the solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1-z \\ 1-z \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+z[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,z\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
